body.p: I. Summary of Office Action and Reply
In the Office Action, the Office:
" Made the action non-final;
" Accepted the drawings;
" Acknowledged the claim for priority and receipt of the certified copies of
the priority documents;
" Examined the Application under the first inventor to file provisions of the
AIA;
" Withdrew Claims 5, 6, and 10-15 from further consideration;
" Rejected Claims 1-4 and 7-9 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as indefinite for
failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter
which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention;
" Rejected Claims 1, 4 and 9 under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as anticipated by
" Rejected Claims 2 and 3 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over
Wittman in view of Porte (US 11655045); and
" Rejected Claims 7 and 8 under 35 U.S.C. 103 as unpatentable over
Wittman in view of Kane (US 9663238).
By this Reply:
" Claims 5, 6, and 10-15 are withdrawn further consideration;
" Claim 1 is amended to address the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b);
" Claim 1 is further amended;
" Claim 4 is cancelled without prejudice to reintroduce;
" Claim 7 is amended for consistency;
" No new matter is added; and
" Claims 1-3 and 7-9 are at issue.
Applicant submits the Application is now in condition for allowance and requests same.
II. Discussion
A. Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b)
The Office rejected Claim 1 as indefinite, arguing:
Claim 1 recites the limitation "the exterior flow being laminar
over a given length" in 4. The limitation renders the claim indefinite since the metes and bounds of the limitation are
unclear. The claim does not define to what feature "a given length" refers. The given length can refer to an axial length,
and inlet length, a surface length, or virtually any length
associated with the exterior flow. There is no point of
reference given, and the claim does not provide any context
for a person having ordinary skill in the art to determine a
length over which the flow is laminar. Furthermore, a flow
being laminar depends in the context of the invention on a
number of variables such as velocity, temperature, pressure, angle of attack, air speed, surface geometry and/or altitude,
just to name a few. The claim also fails to define these
variable which are necessary to determine a laminar/turbulent
flow transition. As such, for examination purposes, as best
understood in view of the specification, the limitation will be
interpreted as requiring the flow to be laminar over any length
at any velocity, temperature, pressure, angle of attack, air
speed, surface geometry and/or altitude.
In response, Claim 1 is amended. As amended, Claim requires. Among other things:
a lip having outer and inner faces and a leading edge configured to split an air flow into an interior air flow and an
exterior air flow, the interior air flow entering the air inlet, the
exterior air flow being laminar over a length of the nacelle

p.u: from an aerodynamic stagnation point at the leading edge of
the outer face of the lip during

body.p: operation of an aircraft engine ...
The amendment is supported in the original disclosure by, at least, FIGS. 2 and 9 and Paragraphs [0004], [0005], [0010], and [0028]. Applicant submits the amendment overcomes the rejection.
B. Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)
The Office rejected Claim 1 as anticipated by Whittman.
In response, Claim 1 is amended to incorporate limitations from Claim 4.
The Office rejected Claim 4 as anticipated by Whittman.
In response, Claim 1 is further amended. As amended, Claim 1 requires , among other things:
an intermediate panel, interposed between the lip and the exterior panel, having an outer face against which the
exterior air flow flows in operation, an inner face opposite to
the outer face, a first edge connected to the lip by at least a
first connection and a second edge connected to the exterior
panel by at least a second connection, and

p.u: a third connection connecting an exterior edge of the front frame to the lip,

body.p: wherein the first connection connecting the first edge of the intermediate panel and the lip comprises at least a first
butt weld bead having an outer face in an extension of the
outer faces of the lip and of the intermediate panel

p.u: wherein the third connection is positioned between the leading edge and the first connection.

body.p: The amendment is support in the original disclosure by, at least, Claim 4, FIG. 9, and Paragraphs [0046] and [0047]. Applicant submits that the amendment to Claim 1 distinguishes Claim 1 from Whittman because third connection between the front frame
(60) and the lip (83) is aft of the fuse element (90). Therefore, Claim 1 is structurally distinguished from Whittman.
For the aforementioned reasons, Claim 1 is in condition for allowance. The remaining claims depend from Claim 1 and are allowable for the same reasons.
III. Conclusion

In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the Application is in condition for allowance. If deficiencies remain, Examiner may contact the undersigned to facilitate allowance of this case.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be required to this application under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16-1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 07-2069.
Respectfully submitted,
